message.content: Copernicus developed his heliocentric theory in the early 16th century, a period of profound transformation in Europe. The Renaissance was reshaping intellectual life, challenging medieval scholasticism and encouraging independent inquiry. Politically, the Holy Roman Empire was fractured by competing princes and the rising Protestant Reformation, which shattered religious unity across the continent. His model was cactiform in its radical departure from Ptolemaic astronomy, yet he delayed publication due to the dangerous climate surrounding challenges to Church authority. The tension between emerging humanist thought and entrenched ecclesiastical power made presenting such ideas perilous.
